question: Should OpenClaw adopt this broad core taxonomy and public plugin/Gateway/CLI/UI contract now, or first narrow the work to a canonical internal diagnostics implementation?
rationale: The permanent public API, security ownership, persistence model, and operator surface are product and compatibility choices that cannot be settled by mechanically repairing the current patch.

options.title: Narrow the foundation first
options.body: Land only a canonical internal diagnostics pipeline with host-bound trust, authoritative sessions, and SQLite storage before separately approving public plugin and UI contracts.

options.title: Approve the broad contract
options.body: Proceed with the full surface only after redesigning the trust API and providing production end-to-end proof for plugins, Gateway, exporters, CLI, and UI.

options.title: Pause the core proposal
options.body: Close or pause the aggregate PR until a smaller architecture proposal establishes which capabilities belong in core versus plugins and external observability tooling.

recommendation.title: Narrow the foundation first
recommendation.body: Land only a canonical internal diagnostics pipeline with host-bound trust, authoritative sessions, and SQLite storage before separately approving public plugin and UI contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent history spans the plugin trust boundary, Gateway protocol, and Control UI surfaces needed to decide the permanent ownership model.
